CITM410 · Academic project

Analysing Business Processes, Alternatives and Operational Controls

Adnan Khan

I developed an academic grocery-fulfilment business case and two supporting airport exercises. The work covers stakeholders, process and data models, timing assumptions, KPIs, redesign options, financial comparison, weighted evaluation and control design.

Tools and environment

Canva; Excel; Google Sheets; rich pictures; SIPOC; swimlanes; data-flow diagrams; KPI definitions; discounted cash-flow and weighted evaluation; control matrices.

Individual CITM410 work by Adnan Khan. June-July 2025. Business and airport details are case assumptions.

Identify the service context and process boundary

I used a rich picture and SIPOC to identify customers, suppliers, store operations, warehouse/delivery participants and technology support. The grocery case describes in-store and online sales. The detailed fulfilment boundary ends at courier handoff; travel to the customer is separate.

Map operating responsibilities and decisions

I built a high-level process map and swimlanes to follow order handling across operating roles. These views identify the sequence and the handoffs, including stock availability and preparation. They provide the baseline against which proposed changes can be reviewed.

Trace information through the process

I developed a data-flow model for order, payment, inventory and supplier information. I also defined named flows by source, destination and purpose. A data-flow view is useful when the problem concerns a missing or incorrect record rather than only the order of tasks.

Calculate normal and delayed fulfilment paths

The assumed normal path totals 33 minutes from order receipt to courier handoff. With 85% immediate availability and a 15% chance of an additional 2,880-minute delay, the expected time is 465 minutes under the additive-delay interpretation.

  • Normal path: receive 2 + payment 3 + inventory 5 + pick 10 + package 6 + label 2 + handoff 5 = 33 minutes.
  • Expected time: 0.85 × 33 + 0.15 × 2,913 = 465 minutes.
  • This is a calculation of case assumptions, not a time study or proof of two-hour delivery.

Define KPIs and how they would be measured

I separated order-to-handoff time, order accuracy, stock availability and inventory-record accuracy. These measures have different denominators and boundaries. The proposed review combines operational timestamps, service/return records and inventory information.

  • Order accuracy: error-free shipped orders / all shipped orders.
  • Availability: eligible orders fillable immediately / eligible orders.
  • The control plan targets at least 90% accuracy and availability, with a separate 98% inventory-record accuracy target. These are proposed targets.

Compare the three operating alternatives

Option 1 retains the status quo. Option 2 clarifies responsibilities and handoffs while improving inventory visibility. Option 3 proposes extensive automation, including AI-assisted demand/reordering and automated fulfilment. The options differ in scope, cost and implementation demands.

Review the financial model on a consistent basis

The case uses five years and a 15% annual discount rate. The corrected full-precision comparison gives NPVs of $335,215.51, $554,305.22 and $1,666,626.76 for Options 1, 2 and 3. These values preserve the source’s Year 1 development-outlay timing.

  • Development outlays: $0, $35,000 and $500,000.
  • Options 2 and 3 assume 5% annual growth in recurring costs and benefits.
  • The ranking depends on estimated benefits and costs; it is not realized profit or a vendor-backed forecast.

Use weighted criteria to support the decision

I compared the options using seven criteria covering financial, operational and strategic considerations. The weighted scores are 23, 63.05 and 88.5. Option 3 ranks first under the chosen ratings and weights.

  • Weights: NPV 25%; development cost 10%; cycle-time reduction 20%; bottlenecks 15%; work in process 10%; customer lead time 10%; competitive advantage 10%.

Link proposed controls to accountable work

The Option 2 control plan includes seven points: order validation, inventory tracking, fulfilment procedures, payment security, courier handoff, label/information checks and KPI review. It also maps validity, completeness and accuracy objectives for information.

State the recommendation and implementation conditions

The academic case recommends Option 3 on its modelled NPV and weighted ranking. Before implementing that concept, the next work would validate data, cost estimates, integrations and exception paths, then test a limited pilot and controls tailored to the chosen option.

  • The Option 2 control matrix is not automatically a complete control design for Option 3.
  • Report realized outcomes separately from targets and modelled benefits.

Apply the method to the airport information-flow case

My airport exercise maps information across passenger, baggage and operating processes. I defined passenger cycle time, screening throughput and immigration-clearance lead time as separate measures. Each needs its own start/end points and evidence.

Extend the airport case into control design

The second airport exercise proposes controls for checkpoints, baggage, ground operations, emergency response, maintenance, reporting and feedback. The matrix links mechanisms to operational and information-quality objectives. These are coursework control proposals rather than deployed airport systems.

What I learned

  • Define the process boundary before interpreting a cycle-time result.
  • A ranking is only as useful as its assumptions and consistent calculations.
  • A control plan needs ownership, evidence and a response when a target is missed.

Source: the full CITM410 portfolio supplied for this project. Evidence is from the original coursework; this edition adds no new lab test results. Repeated captures and earlier drafts are consolidated. Revised design summaries are labelled, and sensitive identifiers are masked.
